youtube.title: Sherlock Holmes' Creator Fell for This Hoax | The Cottingley Fairies
youtube.description:
In 1917, two cousins in Yorkshire photographed "fairies." Arthur Conan Doyle, the creator of Sherlock Holmes, published them in The Strand Magazine in 1920 as evidence fairies were real. In 1983 the cousins confessed: paper cut-outs and hatpins. But Frances insisted until her death that the fifth photo was genuine.

📂 Case File #003: The Cottingley Fairies

Sources: The Strand Magazine, December 1920; the cousins' 1983 confession in The Unexplained; overview: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cottingley_Fairies
Photos: public domain via Wikimedia Commons.
Narration voice: AI.
